Suggestion: make the visibility filter unconditional and drop `mcpApps` from `CreateMcpToolsOptions`.

The spec says the host MUST NOT list tools whose visibility doesn't include `"model"`, with no exception for hosts that haven't advertised the apps extension. A tool tagged `visibility: ["app"]` is never meant for the model, so hiding it when apps are off is still the right behavior (there's no app around to call it either).

That leaves the client factory flag as the single switch for MCP Apps, and removes the "the two must be set together" caveat from DOC.md. Conformant servers only send `_meta.ui` tools after the client advertises the capability anyway, so the factory flag is the real gate.

Not blocking, approving as is. It's just cheaper to collapse this now than after the option is in the published `@cline/core` surface. Feel free to make the change and I can re-review.
Hey! I went this way so as not to break the existing interface, but you're right; it's probably better to do so now rather than later.

This is why boolean parameters are terrible. At the call site, it is impossible to know without scrolling what these mean; and if you mix them up, then no type error results.

It would be better to have something like:

`load({ refresh: true, background: true })`

You can handle defaults with a splat like:

```
args = { refresh: false, background: false, ...actualArgs }
```

Agreed, switched to an options object in 56021e0af: `load({ refresh: true, userInitiated: true })`, with defaults via destructuring (`{ refresh = false, userInitiated = false } = {}`), which does the same thing as the spread. The poll and focus listener now call `load({ refresh: true })`.

🟢 **bug** (low)

The value sent in the `X-Task-ID` request header changed from the task ID to the ulid while the header name (and therefore the contract the Cline backend sees) stayed the same. If the backend treats this header as a task identifier (attribution, rate limiting, server-side joins), the meaning of the header silently changed; for tasks that have no ulid the header is also now empty where it previously always carried a value. This is probably intended as part of "ulid everywhere", but the header name no longer describes its content.

**建议**: Confirm with the backend owner which identifier this header is expected to carry, then either keep sending the task ID or rename the header (e.g. `X-Task-ULID`) so the contract stays unambiguous. If both ids are needed, send them as separate headers.

**证据**: `"X-Task-ID": this.options.ulid || "",`

Begs the question why we can't attach images to question answers, and also what happens if you're in the middle of composing something and the agent asks a question... Seems weird to have that behave differently depending on whether you have attached something or not?

Good questions, both.

**Why no attachments on question answers:** the `ask_question` tool result is a plain string (`AskQuestionExecutor` in `@cline/core` returns `Promise<string>`), so no host can carry images in an answer today: the CLI card's custom-answer field is text only, and the VS Code extension resolves the pending question with the prompt text and drops any images/files that came with it. Supporting it would be a core + sidecar change (an `ask_question` result carrying content blocks the way `read_files` does, plus the desktop attachment plumbing on the answer path). Worth doing, but a separate PR from this fix.

**Consistency:** agreed the attachments branch was odd. Pushed a change so the composer always targets the pending question. Text-only answers the question as before. A message with attachments is now handed back to the composer with an error banner ("Question answers are text only. Remove the attachments to answer, or pick an option first and send the files afterwards.") instead of being silently queued behind the blocked agent or silently dropped. Unit test added for that path.

**Composing mid-question:** the card appearing does not touch your draft; whatever you submit while the card is up is the answer, same as the VS Code extension and legacy Cline where the composer is the answer box. The composer placeholder now says so while a question is pending ("Type an answer to the question above, or pick an option") instead of the busy-state "submit to queue another message" text. If the draft was meant as a follow-up, the agent still receives it as the answer and can act on it, which beats queueing it behind an agent that is blocked waiting on the question (the original bug).
